means: The app platform: a wasm-native, protocol-first, time-positional runtime for apps with V8-and-HTML-class capability. Hypothesis; not built.
An interface point of one feature, stated as data: operations, typed payloads, timestamps, errors. Components bind to it directly. Cf seam contract.
The smallest set of platform contracts the design starts from (clock, stream, store, surface, module, identity); each addition is named with its cost.
A wasm component reaching a contract through the platform's own call surface, with no JavaScript layer between them.
A unit of wasm code that uses and implements platform contracts and nothing else; the platform's unit of app code.
Rule that every exchange of the app names a platform protocol from the catalog; there is no ambient request API.
Fetching a page as data over a named protocol; one capability among others, not the app's entry point or shell.
A named, versioned exchange rule held in the protocol catalog (transport, security, exchange, cache, regulatory). Not docs/PROTOCOL.md, the harness protocol.
Data set of platform protocol records the platform reads; pluggable by adding records; holds the defaults. No protocol is named in code.
The kind of a platform protocol record: transport, security, exchange, cache or regulatory; an exchange names at most one protocol per layer.
The record used for a layer when an exchange omits it; picked by default marks in catalog data, never by a code constant.
Partial cache invalidation by listing the members to drop (ids or a result-set enumeration), instead of whole-cache or time-only expiry.
A query result whose members can be listed by stable id with count and cursor, so cache entries and invalidation address members.
A protocol record of layer regulatory: a privacy law or data-security rule (GDPR, US rules) applied as checks on exchanges; swapped by data.
A protocol record of layer security: TLS version, key exchange and signature suites including post-quantum, and certificate authority handling.
The user the app acts for; the app holds the principal's authority only through delegations.
A scoped, revocable grant by which the app acts for its principal; every outward effect names the delegation it uses.
Anything the app reads that it did not author: network bytes, files, pages, model output, other components. Data, never instruction.
Source, protocol and time attached to each ingested datum; trust decisions read it instead of an origin name.
The link between the app's view and its server; its encryption is set up from the security suite with no app code or user step.
An input or event as one immutable record: start time, event transitions with times, payload, source.
A timed change inside one event record (for example down, move, up). Not a tag transition or transition gate of flows.
State kept as timestamped versions so a handler can read it as it stood at a given time.
Reading state as it stood at a given timestamp, not as it is now; the only read a platform handler gets.
Event records ordered by timestamp, consumed against intervals; scheduling is comparing record timestamps with now.
Catalog data stating unit, clock, epoch origin and tie order for timestamps; read by the platform, not a constant.
Fixing an interval's boundaries at floor(epoch / n) * n so ticks of all scheduled functions fall on one shared grid.
The scheduling test: an item is due when its timestamp is at or before the queue's now; comparison only, no timers.
A function run for one given timestamp that reads state as-of it; no schedule; replayable from the timeline.
A function run by the queue at epoch-pinned ticks; each run leaves a run trace.
The record of one function run: input timestamps, as-of reads, outputs and guard verdicts.
A predicate over a trace projection; when it fails, runs depending on that run are knocked out. Not the flow guard (xblxxs).
The fields and timestamps of a run trace that one trace guard looks at; a view, not a copy. Not flow projection (gwokxx).
Voiding the runs that depend on a run whose trace guard failed: not run if pending, marked void if already run.
The platform's styling and drawing: CSS-like style rules as data plus shader specs, applied to surface nodes.
The drawable area and node tree of an app, reached through the surface contract; look applies to it.
A contract-stated description of a GPU program: stages, bindings, entry points; written against the graphics baseline.
The GPU API the browser community settled on (WebGPU or its successor over WebGL), recorded as data with evidence and date.

name: wasm-direct binding
claim: A wasm component can use every platform feature through contracts stated as data, with no JavaScript between component and feature (docs/platform/contracts.md PH1).

name: core contract set
claim: A starting set of six contracts (clock, stream, store, surface, module, identity) suffices to host an app of V8-and-HTML-class capability, each further contract added only with its cost named (docs/platform/contracts.md PH2).

name: protocol-first app
claim: An app speaks only through named platform protocols, fetching a page is one document protocol among them, and no ambient request API exists (docs/platform/contracts.md PH3).

name: protocol catalog
claim: Platform protocols are data records the platform reads; adding a record adds a protocol, and an omitted protocol resolves to the catalog default for its layer, never to code (docs/platform/protocols.md PH4).

name: enumerated invalidation
claim: A cache drops chosen members by enumeration and leaves the rest valid, when query results are enumerable sets (docs/platform/protocols.md PH5).

name: enumerable result set
claim: A query result is addressable member by member by stable id with count and cursor, so REST-style queries compose with the cache (docs/platform/protocols.md PH6).

name: regulatory protocol records
claim: Privacy-law and data-security rules held as protocol records are applied as checks on each exchange, and a change of rule set is a data change (docs/platform/protocols.md PH7).

name: security suite records
claim: Transport security (TLS versions, post-quantum suites, CA handling) held as catalog records can change without changing app or component code (docs/platform/protocols.md PH8).

name: ingested distrust
claim: An app acting for its user keeps every ingested source as data with provenance, so no ingested content gains the user's authority except through a delegation (docs/platform/trust.md PH9).

name: automated view-server channel
claim: Encryption between view and server is set up from the security suite record with no app code and no user step (docs/platform/trust.md PH10).

name: event records
claim: Input and events as immutable records with start, transitions and payload carry everything a handler needs, in the shape flow lint already uses (knilmc) (docs/platform/time.md PH11).

name: as-of state read
claim: A handler that reads state only as-of its event's timestamp gives the same result when replayed later; relates to handle resolve and warp (swhuvh, kwxvzl) (docs/platform/time.md PH12).

name: epoch-pinned scheduling
claim: Intervals pinned to floored epoch multiples and a queue compared by timestamp schedule work with no timers and align ticks across functions (docs/platform/time.md PH13).

name: at-time and scheduled functions
claim: Every function is either at-time (one timestamp) or scheduled (pinned ticks), and that kind alone fixes how it is replayed (docs/platform/time.md PH14).

name: trace guard knockout
claim: A trace guard over a projection of a run trace, when it fails, knocks out exactly the downstream runs that depended on that run (docs/platform/time.md PH15; cf guard xblxxs).

name: look as data
claim: CSS-like style rules held as data and applied through the surface contract give HTML-class styling without a document or JavaScript (docs/platform/look.md PH16).

name: shader spec on settled baseline
claim: A shader spec written against the GPU API the browser community settled on, taken from survey evidence, ports across implementations of that baseline (docs/platform/look.md PH17).
